findings.claim: Removing `refCleanupMap.get(container)?.()` means a previously registered ref cleanup is never invoked when the `ref` prop changes or is removed, leaking the old ref/cleanup.
findings.rationale: In the `key === 'ref'` branch, the code proceeds to compute a new `cleanup` and (further down) store it in `refCleanupMap`, overwriting the prior entry. With the invocation removed, the old callback ref never gets called with `null` and its cleanup function becomes unreachable, so listeners/observers registered in the old callback ref leak and stale DOM references are retained. The `value == null` case now performs no cleanup at all. Confidence is moderate-high that this is a regression; it would only be correct if an equivalent cleanup call was added on the caller/unmount path, which is not visible in this hunk.
